rv.q: O’Connor is so compelling, in fact, that you’re almost willing to overlook the flaws in a play that, at heart, has the moral sophistication of an RKO Studios B-movie. The director Sam Yates works unbelievably hard — sometimes too hard — at supplying gravitas.
The last 20 minutes go slightly off the rails as the production's melodramatic denouement resorts to explosive bursts of shouting and recrimination following a bloody and tragic bout.
This is a production that packs a powerful punch, resulting in what is confidently a knockout hit.

cn.t: Josh O'Connor's highly anticipated stage return in this Clifford Odets revival generates strong buzz, with critics praising its brooding intensity and timely exploration of the American dream's pitfalls.
